title: rgb(0,0,0) vs rgba(0,0,0,0) in Playwright contrast audits

patterns: color contrast assertion returning false positive

rule.summary: `getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor` returns `rgb(0,0,0)` when an element has NO explicit background — NOT `rgba(0,0,0,0)` as expected. Filtering `rgba(0,0,0,0)` alone produces false positives. You must ALSO check for `rgb(0,0,0)` and then verify via a DOM climb whether the element actually has a background.
rule.details: Playwright's `page.evaluate` with `getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor` returns `rgb(0,0,0)` for elements whose background resolves to the page default (typically body's white or transparent ancestors). The naive filter `filter(c => c !== 'rgba(0,0,0,0)')` misses this. Fix: also filter `rgb(0,0,0)` but ONLY when the element's opacity resolves to 0 at the computed layer, OR implement a DOM climb that walks parents checking for actual background definitions.
rule.check: For any element where `getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor === 'rgb(0,0,0)'`, walk up the DOM tree checking parent `backgroundColor` values. If no ancestor has a defined background, the element is effectively transparent and should be excluded from contrast checks.

evidence.description: False positives in contrast audit due to rgb(0,0,0) not being filtered
evidence.resolution: Added DOM climb with `rgb(0,0,0)` detection in the rgbHex filtering pipeline
